prediction.raw: **0 (Not the asshole)** **Why:** - **Last-minute request is unreasonable:** Your coworker knew his schedule was set a week in advance. If he needed coverage for a memorial (which he *should* have known about earlier), he should have used the official system *immediately* when the schedule was posted—not texted people at 7:30 PM the same day. - **No obligation to cover:** You’re not contractually required to cover shifts outside the system, especially when you’ve already reciprocated a favor ( you covered for him once, and he covered for you). "Being even" is a fair boundary. - **Your mental health matters:** "Hating this job" is a valid reason to refuse extra work. No one should guilt-tr you into sacrificing your well-being for a job you dislike. - **His "Of course not" is on him:** His reaction reflects his own frustration, not your wrongdoing. A memorial is tragic, but last-minute demands on colleagues are inconsiderate—especially when proper channels exist. **Key takeaway:** You acted reasonably. Prioritize your boundaries, and next time, direct him to the official system (or decline firmly: "I’m not available to cover last-minute requests"). 💡
